title: Tumblr Symbols: Copy & Paste Aesthetic Symbols for Your Blog
meta_description: Copy and paste Tumblr aesthetic symbols for a blog title, description or text post: moons ☾ ☽, soft-grunge crosses ✞, the ღ heart, sparkle lines and post dividers.
hero_tagline: Moons, crosses, soft hearts and sparkle lines in the Tumblr aesthetic, grouped by the part of a blog they decorate. Click any symbol to copy it.
intro: Tumblr symbols are the characters that decorated blog titles, blog descriptions and text posts through the pastel and soft-grunge years of Tumblr, and they still mark a blog as Tumblr-style: crescent moons ☾ ☽, crosses like ✞ and †, the Georgian letter ღ standing in for a heart, peace and yin-yang signs, and sparkle lines such as ✧･ﾟ: *✧･ﾟ:*. They are ordinary Unicode characters, so they copy and paste like any other text. The single symbols suit a blog title, the sparkle lines frame a description, and the dividers split a long text post into parts.

sections.label: Moon & Sky
sections.intro: The night-sky set behind countless pastel blog titles. ☾ and ☽ face each other, so they make a pair around a name.

sections.label: Soft Grunge
sections.intro: Crosses, daggers and the ankh, the darker half of the Tumblr look. The full goth set is on the goth and grunge symbols page linked below.

sections.label: Retro Signs
sections.h2: Peace Signs, Smileys and Music Notes
sections.intro: Text smileys and hippie signs from before emoji, still common in Tumblr bios and post tags.

sections.label: Hearts & Flowers
sections.intro: ღ is a letter of the Georgian alphabet that looks like a heart, which is why it turns up in so many blog names.

sections.label: Title Sparkles
sections.h2: Sparkle Lines for a Blog Title or Description
sections.intro: Each button copies the whole string. Put one on each side of a title, like ✧･ﾟ: *✧･ﾟ:* dreamy *:･ﾟ✧*:･ﾟ✧.

sections.label: Dividers
sections.intro: Break a long text post into sections, or close a post with one before the tags.

faq.q: What makes a symbol look Tumblr-style?
faq.a: Mostly the mix: soft night-sky and flower characters like ☾ ✧ ✿ next to darker soft-grunge ones like ✞ and †, with ღ for hearts and sparkle lines around the title. None of these characters belong to Tumblr. The look comes from how its blogs combined them.

faq.q: Why do some symbols show as boxes on my blog?
faq.a: The text you save is the same for everyone, but each visitor's device draws it with its own fonts. A device with no font for a character draws a box in its place. Most of the single symbols here sit in the Miscellaneous Symbols and Dingbats blocks, which have been part of Unicode since its first version in 1991.

faq.q: Can I make the letters of my blog title fancy too?
faq.a: Yes. Symbols decorate around the words, while a font generator changes the letters themselves into bold, cursive or small-caps Unicode. The aesthetic fonts page linked below does that for any title.
